memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: As they fled before Israel on the road down from Beth Horon to Azekah, the Lord hurled large hailstones down on them, and more of them died from the hailstones than were killed by the swords of the Israelites. — Josh 10:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the enemy armies flee, God Himself joins the battle in a dramatic way, hurling great hailstones from heaven upon them. And Scripture records a striking detail: "more of them died from the hailstones than were killed by the swords of the Israelites." God's direct intervention accomplished more than all the swords of Israel combined. The greater part of the victory was unmistakably His doing.

This detail is recorded, it seems, so that no one could ever boast that Israel had won this battle by their own might. When the story was told afterward, it would be clear: the God of heaven fought for His people. The swords of Israel mattered, but the hand of God mattered more. He wanted the glory to be plainly His.

We are prone to over-estimate our own contribution to the good in our lives and under-estimate God's. This verse gently corrects that tendency. So much of what we accomplish, we accomplish only because God is quietly hurling down "hailstones" we never see, doing more behind the scenes than all our visible efforts achieve. When we look honestly, we find God's hand has done the greater part.

The God who commands the very hail and storms is the same God who reigns over all creation for the good of His people. In Christ, we see this same sovereign power exercised in love — even the wind and waves obey Him (Mark 4:41). The Lord of heaven and earth is on the side of His people, and He does far more for us than we could ever do for ourselves. To Him belongs the glory.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to over-credit your own efforts and under-credit God's hidden work?
2. Where might God be doing more behind the scenes than you realise?
3. How does it humble and comfort you that God does the greater part in your battles?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for over-estimating my own strength. Open my eyes to see how much You do behind the scenes, and let the glory for every victory be Yours alone. Amen.
